identification.summary: Storm-0252 is a Microsoft designation (listed as a group in development) whose alias CHATTY SPIDER is CrowdStrike's name [S2]. Secondary reporting equates the activity with Luna Moth, Silent Ransom Group (SRG) and UNC3753, a financially motivated callback-phishing (telephone-oriented attack delivery) data-theft and extortion actor active since at least 2022 [S3][S6].
identification.firstObserved: Secondary reporting: active since at least 2022 [S3]. EclecticIQ-based coverage dates the split from Conti and formation of SRG to March 2022 [S6].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Storm-0252 (group in development); CrowdStrike: CHATTY SPIDER [S2]. The equivalence of Storm-0252/CHATTY SPIDER with Luna Moth, SRG and UNC3753 comes from secondary coverage; vendor cluster boundaries may differ and the Microsoft primary mapping was not opened [S3]. Do not merge facts across vendor clusters without that check.

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor identified. Actor is described as financially motivated eCrime [S7].
attribution.confidence: EclecticIQ, as reported by BleepingComputer, assesses with high confidence that Luna Moth is very likely linked to the actors behind the 2021 BazarCall campaign (Conti/Ryuk) [S6]. This is a vendor assessment, not government attribution. A Russia-based assessment attributed to CrowdStrike could not be verified and was removed.
attribution.basis: EclecticIQ analysis as reported by BleepingComputer, including domain registrations and TTP overlap [S6]; FBI advisories and Mandiant reporting describe the activity but, in the sources gathered, do not attribute it to a nation [S4][S7].

objectives: Financial gain through data theft and extortion; reporting says the group did not deploy ransomware or encrypt files, and demanded seven-figure sums (reportedly $1M to $8M, per a lower-authority aggregator) [S3][S6].

targeting.notes: EclecticIQ's April 2024 to April 2025 window: legal 40.28%, financial services 23.61%, accounting 13.89% of observed victims [S6]. Mandiant reports a January to May 2026 campaign against dozens of US law, professional and financial services organizations [S7].

capabilities.summary: Initial access by callback phishing: invoice or subscription-themed emails prompt victims to call a number [S3]. From March 2025 the FBI says the group shifted to calling targets directly while posing as company IT [S3][S4]. Victims are guided to screen-sharing and install legitimate RMM tools (Zoho Assist, Syncro, AnyDesk, Splashtop, Atera named), then data is exfiltrated with Rclone or WinSCP and an extortion note sent [S3][S6]. EclecticIQ counted at least 37 typosquatted helpdesk-style domains registered via GoDaddy [S6]. Mandiant reports the whole operation from contact to extortion can occur within one day [S7]. Security Affairs and a CSA research note (AI-assisted, not formally reviewed) report a 2026 escalation to physical office visits using USB drives; treat as lower confidence [S8][S9].

campaigns.name: BazarCall callback phishing (predecessor activity)
campaigns.summary: EclecticIQ-based coverage links Luna Moth/SRG to actors behind the 2021 BazarCall campaign that enabled Conti and Ryuk ransomware.

campaigns.name: Formation of Silent Ransom Group
campaigns.summary: As Conti began shutting down, BazarCall actors reportedly separated and formed SRG, shifting to data-theft extortion without encryption.

campaigns.name: Law-firm-heavy callback extortion window
campaigns.summary: EclecticIQ's tracking window April 2024 to April 2025 found legal 40.28%, financial 23.61% and accounting 13.89% of victims.

campaigns.name: Shift to direct IT-impersonation calls
campaigns.summary: FBI said the group changed approach in March 2025, calling targets directly and posing as IT staff to push RMM installation.

campaigns.name: FBI warning on law-firm targeting
campaigns.summary: FBI issued a Private Industry Notification dated 23 May 2025 (per Breached Company summary) warning of the callback campaigns against US law firms.

campaigns.name: Mandiant-tracked campaign against US law firms
campaigns.summary: Google Mandiant attributes a January to May 2026 data-theft extortion campaign against dozens of US legal, professional and financial services organizations to UNC3753 (SRG), published 2026-06-05.

campaigns.name: Reported physical intrusion escalation
campaigns.summary: Secondary and AI-assisted reporting describes operatives visiting offices to plug in USB drives; an FBI FLASH of 26 May 2026 is reported by secondary outlets but was not opened. Mandiant cannot formally attribute every physical intrusion to UNC3753.

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated eCrime group linked to former BazarCall/Conti-era operators by EclecticIQ [S6].
diamond.capability: Callback phishing and vishing, abuse of legitimate RMM tools, Rclone/WinSCP exfiltration, data-only extortion [S3][S6].
diamond.infrastructure: Typosquatted helpdesk domains (37+ via GoDaddy), phone numbers in lure emails, legitimate RMM services [S3][S6].
diamond.victim: US law firms, financial services, accounting and professional services [S6][S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: Profit motive; no state tasking indicated in the sources gathered [S7].
diamond.technology: Help-desk and employee trust in phone-based IT support, and permissive use of RMM software that evades security tooling [S3].

gaps: No Microsoft Threat Intelligence report on Storm-0252 was located or opened; the Storm-0252 to Luna Moth/SRG/UNC3753 equivalence rests on secondary coverage and the Malpedia/Microsoft mapping [S2][S3].
WebFetch was unavailable (DNS failures), so Mandiant, FBI and EclecticIQ primary documents were not opened; claims rely on search-result summaries.

FBI FLASH of 26 May 2026 appears real (reported by AHA and others) but was not opened; physical-intrusion claims rest on secondary reporting and a CSA note stating it was AI-assisted and not formally reviewed [S9].
Ransom demand range of $1M to $8M comes from an aggregator and is not verified.
Individual identities, infrastructure indicators and any Russia nexus are not established in the gathered sources.
Precise EclecticIQ and BleepingComputer publication dates were not confirmed; month-level dates used.
Removed: CrowdStrike CHATTY SPIDER profile and its 'likely Russia-based' assessment; URL did not appear in search results and the claim was not corroborated.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the help-desk process, employee endpoints that permit RMM installation, and file shares holding client data. The actor is criminal, so DoD relevance is mainly through defense-industrial-base law, finance and contracting service providers rather than direct military networks [S6][S7]. STEP 2: The actor is fast (contact to extortion within a day), relies on social engineering rather than exploits, and uses legitimate tools that evade detection [S3][S7]. STEP 3: Template is invoice lure, phone call, RMM install, Rclone/WinSCP exfiltration, extortion note [S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued data-theft extortion of US legal and financial firms. MDCOA is targeting a DIB-adjacent law or contracting firm and extorting by leaking sensitive client or contract data, or the reported move to physical USB intrusions [S8][S9]. Candidate indicators: unsolicited calls from claimed IT staff, new Zoho Assist/Syncro/AnyDesk/Splashtop/Atera installs, Rclone or WinSCP traffic to external IPs, and lookalike [company]-helpdesk domains [S3][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track FBI and Mandiant reporting on SRG/UNC3753 and share RMM-allowlist and helpdesk-impersonation indicators with supported units and DIB partners [S4][S7]. (2) Authorities: the actor is criminal, so response runs through law enforcement and DC3/DIB partnership channels rather than offensive cyberspace authorities. (3) Mission assurance: enforce application allowlisting for RMM tools, verified callback procedures for IT support, and egress monitoring for bulk transfers; protect contractor-held mission data [S3]. (4) Coordination: align with FBI, DC3 and legal/contracting offices on extortion handling and disclosure obligations; include physical-security staff given reported office intrusions, subject to confirmation [S9].
